title: GOD GIVES WHAT HE ASKS FOR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Bezalel, Oholiab and every skilled person to whom the Lord has given skill and ability to know how to carry out all the work of constructing the sanctuary are to do the work just as the Lord has commanded." - Exod 36:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that phrase slowly: "every skilled person to whom the Lord has given skill and ability."

God commanded a sanctuary. Then God supplied the ability to build it. He never issues instructions and leaves us to find our own resources.

This is a quiet comfort for anyone who has looked at something God clearly asks of us — forgiveness, patience, honesty, raising children, staying faithful in a hard marriage — and thought, I do not have what this requires. Left to ourselves, that is true. But God does not leave us to ourselves.

Notice the balance in the verse, though. God gives the skill; the people still have to do the work. Divine enabling does not remove human effort. Paul held both together: work out your salvation, for it is God who works in you (Phil 2:12-13).

And notice the boundary: "just as the Lord has commanded." Their skill was not licence to improvise. Great ability submitted to God's design.

Whatever God has called you to today, He has already made provision for it. His divine power has given us everything we need for a godly life (2 Pet 1:3). Start with what He has put in your hands, and do it His way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God asked of you that feels beyond your ability?
2. Do you use your abilities within God's instructions or according to your own preference?
3. Where do you need to stop waiting and start working with what He has given?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You never command without providing. Give me courage to begin, and grace to do it Your way. Amen.
